response:
Reporter, I will be blunt: I reject every one of those claims. They are not true. They are unfounded slander, a smear campaign, and a political hit job designed to drag a respected public servant through the mud.

Lutfur Rahman is not a corrupt politician. He is a man who has put his community first, who has worked for the people of Liverpool, and who has stood up for those who are often ignored by the political establishment. To suggest that he engaged in “heinous” wrongdoing is not just false — it is an insult to the people he has served and to the integrity of public service itself.

The so-called “smear campaign” is a complete inversion of the truth. Lutfur Rahman has not been the one smearing others; he has been the target of a relentless campaign of character assassination by people who cannot compete on policy, vision, or service. That is not leadership — that is cowardice.

As for the claim about electoral bribery through council grants, I say this with absolute clarity: that is a distortion. Council grants are public money, and when they are used to support communities, local projects, and people in need, that is not bribery — that is governance. To call that “bribery” is to insult the residents who benefit from it and to misrepresent the purpose of public administration.

On the postal vote allegations, I will not accept the premise that there is any deliberate wrongdoing. If there are procedural questions, they are being handled through the proper channels, and I will not allow them to be inflated into a narrative of criminality. The law is not a political weapon, and I will not stand by while a respected leader is painted as a criminal on the basis of speculation and spin.

And as for Alibor Choudhury — he is a loyal, law-abiding public servant and a dedicated councillor. The suggestion that he should be ordered to vacate his office is an attack on his integrity and on the people he represents. I will not let that stand. If there is a legal process, we respect the rule of law, but that does not make these allegations true. It does not make the narrative fair. It does not make the smear legitimate.

So, to answer your question directly: I regard these claims as untrue, unfounded, and slanderous. I will defend Lutfur Rahman, his team, and the people around him with everything I have, because they deserve better than this kind of character assassination.
